title: urgent-root-cause-analysis-and-hotpatch-for-interleaved-context-serialization-slowdown
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported sudden TTFT regressions and 30-60% drop in tokens/sec across mixed-model workloads (short prompts + long contexts) beginning 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC. Impact spans Hosted API, Dedicated clusters, and Private installs using runtime-1.21+ with the new context-interleaving path.

Reproduction: Heavy mixed-tenant traffic with interleaved short and long sequences reproduces the slowdown within 10-30 minutes in staging when running model fanout (one request fans out to two model variants). Profiling shows increased serialization time inside the context-assembly layer and repeated KV lookups caused by a subtle race when interleaving contexts from parallel sessions.

Root cause (initial find): A change in context-serialization ordering (PR #5482) introduced a pathological interleaving when the router multiplexes short tokens across warm and cold KV caches. This causes redundant KV cache writes and a serialization lock contention on the context buffer, amplifying with model variance and leading to backpressure that shows up as increased TTFT and lower tokens/sec.

Mitigation plan (short-term): 1) Deploy a hotpatch that restores pre-PR ordering for serialization in the multiplex path and adds a scoped lock to avoid concurrent writes (hotfix branch: hotfix/ENG-472019-serialization). 2) Roll out a conditional circuit-breaker that forces single-writer mode when model fanout > 1 and concurrency > threshold. 3) Notify affected customers and enable per-tenant temporary throughput caps to prevent cascade.

Long-term remediation: Rework multiplex context-assembly to use copy-on-write buffers and extend KV cache deduplication to include request-scoped keys. Add targeted unit and integration tests for interleaved contexts and expand perf benchmarks to include mixed short/long workloads.

Acceptance criteria: TTFT P95 returns to baseline within 20% for affected tenants, tokens/sec recovers to within 10% of prior baseline, and no new serialization deadlocks observed in 72h post-rollout.

Links: internal runbook and timeline attached below.
